messages.speaker: Dev
messages.text: Made the mushroom risotto tonight and it came out gluey. What did I do wrong?

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: Did you rinse the rice first? Washing arborio strips the starch you actually want.

messages.speaker: Dev
messages.text: I did rinse it. Also I dumped all the stock in at once because I was in a hurry.

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: There it is. Add the stock a ladle at a time and stir. That is what releases starch slowly and gives you creaminess without glue.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Also take it off the heat while the grains still have a little bite. It keeps cooking in the pan.

messages.speaker: Dev
messages.text: Noted. How much stock for 300g of rice?

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: Roughly a litre, but go by texture rather than the number. Some days the rice drinks more.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: On a different note, my bread keeps coming out dense. Crumb is tight and it barely rises.

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: How warm is your kitchen? Dough proves painfully slowly under about 20 degrees.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Maybe 17 at the moment, the heating has been off.

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: Then give it longer, not more yeast. Two hours at 17 degrees is nowhere near two hours at 24.

messages.speaker: Dev
messages.text: The oven with just the light on is a decent proving box, about 26 degrees.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That is a good trick, I will try it tomorrow.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Can someone settle an argument. Do you salt pasta water before or after it boils?

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: It makes no real difference to the pasta. Salting after it boils just avoids pitting the bottom of the pan.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: The amount matters far more than the timing. It should taste properly seasoned, not faintly salty.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: How much is properly seasoned in grams?

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: About 10g per litre of water. Any less and the pasta is bland no matter what sauce you put on it.

messages.speaker: Dev
messages.text: What are we all cooking for the meetup on Saturday?

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: I will bring a dal, it travels well and reheats without going strange.

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: I will do a tray of roasted vegetables and a big salad. Two people coming are vegetarian.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Then I will handle bread and something sweet. Sourdough if the proving goes better this time.

messages.speaker: Dev
messages.text: I can bring the risotto if I have redeemed myself by then.

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: Risotto does not survive a car journey. Bring something that likes sitting around instead.

messages.speaker: Dev
messages.text: Fair. A slow cooked ragu then, that only improves overnight.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Does anyone have a nut allergy coming? I want to know before I put cashews in anything.

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: One of Sam's friends cannot have peanuts. Tree nuts are fine but label the dish anyway.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Confirmed, peanuts only. I will bring cards so every dish says what is in it.

messages.speaker: Priya
messages.text: Perfect. What time are we starting?

messages.speaker: Nora
messages.text: Doors at six, eating around seven. Come earlier if you need oven space.

messages.speaker: Dev
messages.text: I will need the oven for twenty minutes to reheat, so I will get there at half five.
